category: CFD: Single-Phase Flow Features, Numerics, Results Variables, Studies and Rotating Machinery
description: Boundary and domain features of the Laminar/Creeping/Turbulent Flow interfaces (walls, inlets, outlets, fans, grilles, screens, sources), CFD numerics (discretization, stabilization, pseudo time stepping, boundary-layer meshing), verified postprocessing variables (velocity, stress, y+, drag/lift, pressure drop, residence time), CFD study types (Frozen Rotor, Phase Initialization) and Mixer Module rotating-machinery features.

tools.name: Wall: Slip, Navier Slip, Slip Velocity and Leaking Wall (Single-Phase Flow)
tools.description: Alternative Boundary condition options of the Wall node besides the default No slip. Slip imposes only no penetration (u·n = 0); Navier slip adds a tangential friction stress with slip length β (useful for moving contact lines); Slip velocity models micro/nano-scale Maxwell viscous slip and thermal creep; Leaking wall prescribes a fluid velocity through a perforated wall. Slip velocity, Leaking wall and Navier slip are only available for laminar flow.
tools.usage: Laminar Flow > Wall > Boundary Condition; Java: physics("spf").feature("wallbc1").set("BoundaryCondition", "Slip")

parameters.name: BoundaryCondition
parameters.description: NoSlip (default), Slip, Slip velocity, Leaking wall or Navier slip (turbulent interfaces offer only NoSlip/Slip).

parameters.name: NavierSlip / beta / beta_factor
parameters.description: Slip length as factor of minimum element length (hmin, default factor 0.5) or user-defined β.

parameters.name: UseViscousSlip / SlipLengthOption / Ls / alphav / lambda
parameters.description: Slip length user defined or from Maxwell's model with tangential momentum accommodation coefficient and mean free path.

parameters.name: UseThermalCreep / sigmat
parameters.description: Thermal creep with thermal slip coefficient (default 0.75).

parameters.name: uleak
parameters.description: Fluid velocity through a leaking wall.

tools.notes: Slip is often used on far-field or symmetry-like walls of external flow boxes. For rarefied gases in the slip regime prefer the Slip Flow interface. Property names verified in COMSOL 6.4.

tools.name: Wall Movement: Sliding Wall and Moving Wall (Single-Phase Flow)
tools.description: Wall Movement section of the Wall node describing wall motion relative to the lab frame. Translational velocity is detected automatically from a moving frame (ALE), can be fixed to zero, or set manually for small oscillations; Sliding wall prescribes a tangential velocity like a conveyor belt or rotating cylinder without moving the boundary. Swirl flow in 2D axisymmetry also allows an azimuthal wall velocity.
tools.usage: Laminar/Turbulent Flow > Wall > Wall Movement; Java properties TranslationalVelocityOption, utr, SlidingWall, uvwwall

parameters.name: TranslationalVelocityOption
parameters.description: AutomaticFromFrame (default), ZeroFixedWall or Manual (utr).

parameters.name: SlidingWall
parameters.description: 1 activates the sliding wall velocity (3D vector projected to the tangent plane, 2D scalar U_w).

parameters.name: uvwwall
parameters.description: Velocity of the sliding wall.

tools.notes: A Manual translational velocity does not move the mesh; add a Moving Mesh/Deforming Domain if the wall position changes.

tools.name: Wall Roughness, Sand and Generic (Turbulent Flow Wall Functions)
tools.description: When the wall treatment is Wall functions, the Wall and Interior Wall nodes can apply wall roughness: the Sand roughness model based on Nikuradse's experiments with an equivalent sand-grain height, or a Generic roughness with roughness height and a roughness parameter. Roughness shifts the logarithmic velocity profile and raises friction and pressure drop, which matters for pipes, channels, ship hulls and terrain.
tools.usage: Turbulent Flow (wall functions) > Wall > Apply wall roughness; Java: feature("wallbc1").set("ApplyWallRoughness", "1")

parameters.name: ApplyWallRoughness
parameters.description: 1 enables roughness (wall-function treatment only).

parameters.name: RoughnessModel
parameters.description: SandRoughness (kseq, default 3.2 µm) or GenericRoughness (ks and Cs, default 0.26).

tools.notes: Roughness is not available with Low Re wall treatment; the first cell must be larger than the roughness height.

tools.name: Inlet: Velocity Condition (Single-Phase Flow)
tools.description: Default Inlet boundary condition prescribing either a normal inflow speed U0 (u = -n U0) or a full velocity vector u0. For turbulent interfaces the Turbulence Conditions section then defines k, ε, ω etc., and for LES/DES synthetic turbulence can be added. Combine it with a pressure outlet for a well-posed problem.
tools.usage: Laminar Flow > Inlet > Boundary Condition: Velocity; Java: physics("spf").create("inl1", "InletBoundary", 2); feature("inl1").set("U0in", ...)

parameters.name: BoundaryCondition
parameters.description: Velocity (default) | Pressure | MassFlow | FullyDevelopedFlow.

parameters.name: ComponentWise
parameters.description: NormalInflowVelocity (U0in) or VelocityFieldComponentWise (u0 vector).

parameters.name: includeSyntheticTurb
parameters.description: LES/DES synthetic fluctuations.

tools.notes: A parabolic expression gives a developed laminar profile; otherwise the flat profile needs an entrance length. Property names verified in COMSOL 6.4.

tools.name: Inlet: Pressure Condition (Single-Phase Flow)
tools.description: Inlet option specifying the normal stress (approximately the pressure), either static or total pressure for incompressible flow, with optional flow direction control and backflow suppression. It is used when a pressure difference, not a flow rate, drives the flow, for example gravity-fed or pump-pressurized systems.
tools.usage: Laminar/Turbulent Flow > Inlet > Boundary Condition: Pressure; Java: feature("inl1").set("BoundaryCondition", "Pressure"); set("p0", ...)

parameters.name: PressureType
parameters.description: StaticPressure or TotalPressure (incompressible only); AverageTotalPressure for an averaged total pressure.

parameters.name: p0
parameters.description: Pressure value; absolute if the reference pressure is 0, otherwise gauge.

parameters.name: SuppressBackflow
parameters.description: Locally adjusts pressure to reduce outflow through the inlet (default on).

parameters.name: FlowDirection / d_u
parameters.description: NormalFlow or user-defined inflow direction.

parameters.name: CompensateForHydrostaticPressure
parameters.description: Adds the hydrostatic pressure when gravity is included.

tools.notes: Specifying pressure at both inlet and outlet is valid; specifying velocity at both usually is not.

tools.name: Inlet: Mass Flow and Standard Flow Rate (Single-Phase Flow)
tools.description: Inlet option prescribing an integrated normal mass flow rate, a pointwise mass flux, a standard volumetric flow rate (SEMI E12-0303, from standard density or standard p and T) or a flow in SCCM units. The mass flow is assumed parallel to the boundary normal. It is common in semiconductor gas delivery, burners and reactors where controllers set a mass or standard flow.
tools.usage: Laminar/Turbulent Flow > Inlet > Boundary Condition: Mass flow; Java: feature("inl1").set("BoundaryCondition", "MassFlow"); set("MassFlowType", ...)

parameters.name: MassFlowType
parameters.description: MassFlowRate (mfr) | PointWiseMassFlux (Mf) | StandardFlowRate (stdmfr) | StandardFlowRateSCCM (sccmmfr).

parameters.name: StandardFlowRateDefinedBy
parameters.description: StandardRho (standard molar volume mnst) or StandardP (Pst, Tst).

parameters.name: Mn
parameters.description: Mean molar mass of the gas for standard flow rates.

parameters.name: multipleInlets
parameters.description: Apply condition on each disjoint selection separately (default on).

parameters.name: Channel thickness
parameters.description: 2D models need the out-of-plane thickness d_bc.

tools.notes: Postprocessing integrals are not automatically scaled by the 2D channel thickness.

tools.name: Inlet: Fully Developed Flow (Single-Phase Flow)
tools.description: Inlet option that computes the fully developed profile of a virtual infinite channel extruded from the (flat) inlet cross section, controlled by average velocity, volumetric flow rate or average pressure. It works for laminar and RANS-EVM turbulent flow (turbulence variables are solved consistently) and replaces the older laminar inflow option. It avoids long entrance sections upstream of the region of interest.
tools.usage: Laminar/Turbulent Flow > Inlet > Boundary Condition: Fully developed flow; Java: set("BoundaryCondition", "FullyDevelopedFlow"); set("FullyDevelopedFlowOption", "Uav")

parameters.name: FullyDevelopedFlowOption
parameters.description: Uav (average velocity Uavfdf) | V0 (flow rate V0fdf) | p0av (average pressure p0avfdf).

parameters.name: Entrance thickness D_z
parameters.description: Out-of-plane thickness in 2D when the flow rate is given.

parameters.name: CompensateForHydrostaticPressurefdf
parameters.description: Hydrostatic compensation when gravity is included.

tools.notes: The inlet boundary must be flat; any volume force must be roughly aligned with the inlet normal. Not available for RANS-RSM models.

tools.name: Outlet: Pressure Condition and Backflow Suppression (Single-Phase Flow)
tools.description: Default Outlet condition prescribing the normal stress (≈ static or total pressure) with zero tangential stress. Suppress backflow (on by default) locally raises the pressure to prevent fluid from entering, which stabilizes recirculation near the outlet; Normal flow forces the flow to leave perpendicular to the boundary.
tools.usage: Laminar/Turbulent Flow > Outlet > Boundary Condition: Pressure; Java: physics("spf").create("out1", "OutletBoundary", 2); set("p0", ...)

parameters.name: p0 / PressureType
parameters.description: Static (default) or Total pressure; AverageTotalPressure applies the total pressure in averaged form (default).

parameters.name: SuppressBackflow
parameters.description: Default 1.

parameters.name: NormalFlow
parameters.description: No tangential velocity instead of no tangential stress.

parameters.name: CompensateForHydrostaticPressure
parameters.description: Adds ρgz when gravity is on and reduced pressure is off.

tools.notes: If something interesting happens at the outlet (vortex shedding, jets), extend the domain instead of relying on backflow suppression.

tools.name: Outlet: Fully Developed Flow, Velocity and Mass Flow (Single-Phase Flow)
tools.description: Alternative Outlet options: Fully developed flow imposes the profile of a virtual extruded channel with prescribed average velocity, flow rate or average pressure; Velocity prescribes normal outflow speed or a vector; Mass flow fixes the integrated outflow (mass, standard or SCCM). Useful for split flows where the flow distribution between several outlets is known.
tools.usage: Laminar/Turbulent Flow > Outlet > Boundary Condition; Java: feature("out1").set("BoundaryCondition", "FullyDevelopedFlow" | "Velocity" | "MassFlow")

parameters.name: FullyDevelopedFlowOption
parameters.description: Uav | V0 | p0av (default p0av for outlets).

parameters.name: ComponentWise / U0out
parameters.description: Normal outflow velocity or velocity field.

parameters.name: MassFlowType / mfr
parameters.description: Mass flow rate specification.

tools.notes: At least one boundary must fix the pressure level (pressure outlet, open boundary or Pressure Point Constraint).

tools.name: Boundary Stress (Single-Phase Flow)
tools.description: General traction boundary condition: General stress sets the total stress vector F, Normal stress sets only the normal component, and Normal stress, normal flow additionally sets zero tangential velocity. For turbulent flow the boundary type (open boundary, inlet or outlet) decides how turbulence variables are treated. Use it for free surfaces with known loads or non-standard outflows.
tools.usage: Laminar/Turbulent Flow > Boundary Stress; Java: physics("spf").create("bs1", "BoundaryStress", 2)

parameters.name: BoundaryCondition
parameters.description: GeneralStress (Fbnd) | NormalStress (f0) | NormalStressNormalFlow (f0).

parameters.name: TurbBndType
parameters.description: OpenBoundary | Inlet | Outlet for turbulence variables.

parameters.name: CompensateForHydrostaticPressure
parameters.description: Adds hydrostatic pressure with gravity.

tools.notes: Implicitly constrains pressure: p ≈ -n·F when ∂u_n/∂n is small.

tools.name: Fan (Single-Phase Flow)
tools.description: Exterior-boundary fan condition acting as an inlet or outlet whose flow rate follows a static pressure curve (linear between no-flow pressure and free delivery, tabulated data, or a user-defined function of the flux spf.V0). It avoids meshing the fan blades in electronics cooling and ventilation models; an optional swirl on the downstream side can be specified.
tools.usage: Laminar/Turbulent Flow > Fan; Java: physics("spf").create("fan1", "ExtFan", 2)

parameters.name: FlowDirection
parameters.description: Inlet or Outlet.

parameters.name: FlowCondition
parameters.description: StaticPressureCurveLinear (pnf no-flow pressure, V0fd free delivery flow) | StaticPressureCurveData | StaticPressureCurveUserDefined.

parameters.name: pinput / pexit
parameters.description: Pressure at the fan inlet or outlet side.

parameters.name: NormalFlowDirection
parameters.description: NormalFlow, SwirlFlow (rotation speed f, swirl ratio c_sf) or user-defined direction.

tools.notes: The fan curve uses the flux across the whole selection; do not use one Fan node on disjoint boundaries. Java type id is ExtFan.

tools.name: Interior Fan (Single-Phase Flow)
tools.description: Fan condition on an interior boundary (slit) where velocity and pressure may be discontinuous: mass flow is conserved across it and the pressure jump follows a static pressure curve or the flux is prescribed. It represents axial fans inside enclosures or ducts without resolving the rotor. Together with Nonisothermal Flow the thermal effects are also coupled.
tools.usage: Laminar/Turbulent Flow > Interior Fan; Java: physics("spf").create("ifan1", "InteriorFan", 2)

parameters.name: FlowDirection
parameters.description: AlongNormalVector or OppositeToNormalVector.

parameters.name: FlowCondition
parameters.description: StaticPressureCurveLinear | Data | UserDefined | PrescribedFlux (V0pf).

parameters.name: prescribeFlowDirection
parameters.description: Enforce normal, swirl or user-defined direction at the fan outlet side.

tools.notes: The interior boundary must separate two fluid domains (use a slit or an internal face).

tools.name: Grille (Single-Phase Flow)
tools.description: Inlet/outlet condition modeling the pressure drop of a grille covering an opening: quadratic loss (Δp = qlc·V0²), a predefined grille type (wire gauze, square mesh, perforated plate with solidity) or a loss coefficient K (Δp = 0.5 K ρ u_n²). Common for vents of electronic cabinets and building ventilation.
tools.usage: Laminar/Turbulent Flow > Grille; Java: physics("spf").create("gr1", "Grille", 2)

parameters.name: FlowDirection
parameters.description: Inlet (pinput) or Outlet (pexit).

parameters.name: FlowCondition
parameters.description: QuadraticLoss (qlc) | GrilleType (GrilleType, solidity, wireDiameter) | LossCoefficient (Kloss).

parameters.name: Turbulence conditions
parameters.description: Inlet turbulence variables for turbulent interfaces.

tools.notes: For turbulent interfaces only quadratic loss and loss coefficient are available.

tools.name: Screen (Single-Phase Flow)
tools.description: Interior boundary condition treating wire gauzes, square meshes and perforated plates as thin permeable barriers with correlations for the resistance coefficient and the refraction (flow-turning) coefficient. It captures pressure drop and flow deflection through inclined screens, filters and flow straighteners without meshing the mesh wires.
tools.usage: Laminar/Turbulent Flow > Screen (interior boundaries only); Java: physics("spf").create("sc1", "Screen", 2)

parameters.name: ScreenType
parameters.description: WireGauze | SquareMesh | PerforatedPlate | userdef (resistance coefficient K).

parameters.name: solidity
parameters.description: Blocked-to-total area ratio σ_s (default 0.5).

parameters.name: wireDiameter
parameters.description: Wire diameter for wire gauze.

parameters.name: Refraction
parameters.description: WireGauze correlation or user-defined refraction coefficient η.

tools.notes: Requires the CFD Module. With Nonisothermal Flow the screen also conserves energy across the barrier.

tools.name: Vacuum Pump (Single-Phase Flow)
tools.description: Outlet condition modeling the effective volume flow rate drawn by a vacuum pump from its performance curve versus suction pressure: linear between ultimate pressure and ambient, tabulated data or a user expression of the averaged suction pressure (spf.pmp1.pAverage). It is used for load-lock pump-down, CVD chambers and degassing systems in the continuum regime.
tools.usage: Laminar/Turbulent Flow > Vacuum Pump; Java: physics("spf").create("pmp1", "VacuumPump", 2)

parameters.name: CurveType
parameters.description: VacuumPumpPerformanceCurveLinear (pult, V0amb, pamb) | ...Data (spdata/prdata table) | ...UserDefined.

parameters.name: InterpolationType
parameters.description: Linear, piecewise cubic or cubic spline for data curves.

parameters.name: VolumeFlowRateUnit / SuctionPressureUnit
parameters.description: Units of the tabulated curve (cfm, l/s, m^3/h; Pa, mbar, Torr, ...).

tools.notes: For Knudsen numbers above about 0.1 use the Molecular Flow Module (Free Molecular Flow or Transitional Flow) instead.

tools.name: Interior Wall (Single-Phase Flow)
tools.description: Wall condition applied on both sides of an interior boundary, allowing velocity, pressure and turbulence discontinuities so thin baffles, plates and blades need not be meshed as solids. It supports no slip, slip, Navier slip, moving walls and (with wall functions) roughness, for laminar and turbulent flow.
tools.usage: Laminar/Turbulent Flow > Interior Wall; Java: physics("spf").create("iwbc1", "InteriorWallBC", 2)

parameters.name: BoundaryCondition
parameters.description: NoSlip (default) or Slip (laminar also Navier slip).

parameters.name: TranslationalVelocityOption
parameters.description: AutomaticFromFrame, ZeroFixedWall or Manual.

parameters.name: ApplyWallRoughness
parameters.description: Roughness with wall functions.

tools.notes: Needs the boundaries to be interior (e.g., created as embedded surfaces). Use Interior Wetted Wall for two-phase flow.

tools.name: Porous Interface (Single-Phase Flow)
tools.description: Interface condition between domains with different porosity (free fluid/porous or porous/porous) that accounts for the jump in porosity: continuity of velocity with stress, porosity-corrected stress, or porosity-corrected stress with a pressure loss (user coefficients or Borda–Carnot with vena contracta models). It gives physically correct pressure jumps at filter faces and packed-bed entrances.
tools.usage: Laminar/Turbulent Flow (porous domains enabled) or Brinkman > Porous Interface; Java: physics("spf").create("pi1", "PorousInterface", 2)

parameters.name: continuityConditions
parameters.description: velocityAndStress | velocityAndPorosityCorrectedStress (default) | velocityAndPorosityCorrectedStressWithLoss.

parameters.name: pressureLossModel
parameters.description: userDef or bordaCarnot; venaContractaModel userDef or Weisbach.

parameters.name: constrainWallDistance
parameters.description: Optional wall-distance constraint on the interface for turbulent models.

tools.notes: Flow Continuity on pairs with different porosity applies the same condition (without density-jump correction).

tools.name: Flow Continuity (Single-Phase Flow Pair)
tools.description: Pair condition making the flow field continuous across an identity pair of nonconforming meshes, typically the rotor–stator interface of a rotating machinery assembly or glued assembly parts. Nonoverlapping parts fall back to the Wall condition.
tools.usage: Laminar/Turbulent Flow > Pairs > Flow Continuity (requires Form Assembly + Identity Pair); Java: physics("spf").create("fcont1", "Continuity", 2), then select the identity pair in the Pair Selection section

parameters.name: Pair selection
parameters.description: Identity pair(s) between the two parts.

parameters.name: Fallback
parameters.description: Wall is applied on nonoverlapping regions unless another feature is selected.

tools.notes: Low-Re wall treatment in k-ω/SST/low-Re k-ε is incompatible with a Wall fallback whose overlap changes in time; set the Wall to Nonpair region.

tools.name: Average Pressure (Single-Phase Flow)
tools.description: Global constraint that sets the average pressure over the selected flow domains when no boundary condition fixes the pressure level (for example closed cavities or fully periodic domains). If the reference pressure is zero it sets the average absolute pressure.
tools.usage: Laminar/Turbulent Flow > Average Pressure (domain constraint)

parameters.name: Average pressure p_ave
parameters.description: Target average (gauge or absolute) pressure.

tools.example:
// GUI: Laminar Flow > right-click > Average Pressure, select all fluid domains, p_ave = 0
// For large 3D models prefer: model.component("comp1").physics("spf").create("prpc1", "PressurePointConstraint", 0);
tools.notes: It couples all pressure degrees of freedom, which can increase memory and make the system ill-conditioned; a Pressure Point Constraint is usually preferable.

tools.name: Point Mass Source and Line Mass Source (Single-Phase Flow)
tools.description: Mass sources concentrated on a point (mass flux in kg/s) or an edge/line (kg/(m·s)) that inject or remove fluid without resolving the inlet geometry, for example small nozzles, bubblers or wells in a free-flow model. A domain Mass Source is also available with porous domains. Sources on a symmetry plane act with doubled strength.
tools.usage: Laminar/Turbulent Flow > Points > Point Mass Source or Edges > Line Mass Source; Java: physics("spf").create("pms1", "PointMassSource", 0) / create("lms1", "LineMassSource", 1)

parameters.name: Mass flux
parameters.description: Positive values eject mass into the domain, negative remove mass.

parameters.name: Selection
parameters.description: Points (Point Mass Source) or edges (Line Mass Source, incl. symmetry axis in 2D axisymmetry).

tools.notes: Requires one of: CFD, Battery Design, Chemical Reaction Engineering, Corrosion, Electrochemistry, Electrodeposition, Fuel Cell & Electrolyzer, Microfluidics, Pipe Flow or Subsurface Flow Module. Point sources give singular velocities locally; evaluate results away from the point.

tools.name: Volume Force (Single-Phase Flow)
tools.description: Domain node adding a body force per unit volume F to the momentum equation (N/m³), for example Lorentz forces in MHD, electroosmotic or dielectrophoretic body forces, porous resistances or a user-defined buoyancy term. Several Volume Force nodes on a domain are summed.
tools.usage: Laminar/Turbulent Flow > Volume Force; Java: physics("spf").create("vf1", "VolumeForce", 3); feature("vf1").set("F", new String[]{...})

parameters.name: F_src
parameters.description: userdef or fromCommonDef (a force computed by another interface).

parameters.name: F
parameters.description: Force vector components (N/m³).

tools.notes: For plain gravity use Include gravity instead, which handles hydrostatic pressure compensation in boundary conditions.

tools.name: Gravity and Reduced Pressure (Single-Phase Flow)
tools.description: Include gravity adds a global Gravity node with the acceleration vector (default -g_const in z for 3D/axisymmetric, -y in 2D). Use reduced pressure changes the dependent variable to p minus the hydrostatic part, which improves accuracy for tall domains with small density variations; boundary pressures can then be given without the hydrostatic contribution.
tools.usage: Single-Phase Flow interface > Physical Model > Include gravity (+ Use reduced pressure); Java: prop("PhysicalModelProperty").set("IncludeGravity", "1")

parameters.name: IncludeGravity
parameters.description: 1 adds the Gravity node (grav1).

parameters.name: UseReducedPressure
parameters.description: Solve for reduced pressure.

parameters.name: rref
parameters.description: Reference position for the hydrostatic pressure.

parameters.name: Project gravity vector on rotation axis
parameters.description: Available when combined with Rotating frame.

tools.notes: With gravity on and reduced pressure off, inlet/outlet/open boundaries by default compensate for hydrostatic pressure.

tools.name: Rotating Frame (Single-Phase Flow)
tools.description: Global feature added when Rotating frame is selected in the Physical Model section: the equations are written in a frame rotating with constant or time-dependent angular velocity, adding Coriolis, centrifugal and Euler forces. It suits fully rotating systems (spinning disks, rotating channels, centrifuges, lab-on-a-CD) where no stationary part exists.
tools.usage: Single-Phase Flow interface > Physical Model > Rotating frame; Java: prop("PhysicalModelProperty").set("RotatingFrame", "1"); feature("rtfr1") is RotatingFrameFD

parameters.name: Axis of rotation
parameters.description: x, y, z (default) or user-defined axis with base point (3D); out-of-plane axis in 2D.

parameters.name: Rotation speed
parameters.description: Angular velocity, revolutions per time or user-defined rotation angle α(t).

parameters.name: Rotational direction
parameters.description: Counterclockwise (default) or clockwise.

tools.notes: For machines with both rotating and stationary parts use a Rotating Domain with Frozen Rotor or Time Dependent studies instead.

tools.name: Physical Model Settings: Compressibility and Stokes Flow (spf)
tools.description: Interface-level Physical Model section of Laminar/Turbulent Flow, in Java prop("PhysicalModelProperty"). It chooses incompressible, weakly compressible (density from temperature) or compressible (Ma < 0.3) formulations, neglects inertia (Stokes/creeping flow), enables porous domains, gravity and rotating frame, and holds the reference pressure and temperature.
tools.usage: Select the spf node > Physical Model; Java: model.component("comp1").physics("spf").prop("PhysicalModelProperty").set(name, value)

parameters.name: Compressibility
parameters.description: Incompressible | WeaklyCompressible | CompressibleMALT03.

parameters.name: StokesFlowProp
parameters.description: 1 = neglect inertial term (Stokes flow).

parameters.name: pref / Tref
parameters.description: Reference pressure level (default 1 atm) and reference temperature (293.15 K).

parameters.name: EnablePorousMediaDomains / IncludeGravity / RotatingFrame / UseReducedPressure
parameters.description: Switches for porous domains, gravity, rotating frame and reduced pressure.

tools.notes: Property names and values verified in COMSOL 6.4. When pref is nonzero the interface solves for gauge pressure p and material properties use spf.pA = p + pref.

tools.name: Discretization P1+P1 and P2+P1 (Single-Phase Flow)
tools.description: Choice of shape functions for velocity and pressure: the default P1+P1 (equal-order linear) relies on Galerkin least-squares stabilization and is cheap and robust for turbulent and large models; P2+P1 (Taylor–Hood) or higher orders are inf-sup stable and more accurate for laminar and creeping flow at the same mesh. In Java this is prop("ShapeProperty") order_fluid.
tools.usage: spf node > Discretization (Show More Options > Advanced Physics Options); Java: physics("spf").prop("ShapeProperty").set("order_fluid", "2")

parameters.name: order_fluid
parameters.description: 1 (P1+P1, default) up to 5; order n gives Pn+P(n-1) for n>1.

parameters.name: valueType
parameters.description: real or complex (complex for frequency-domain linearizations).

tools.notes: Higher order increases DOFs by roughly a factor 4 in 3D; keep P1+P1 for turbulence models and use a finer mesh instead.

tools.name: Consistent and Inconsistent Stabilization (Fluid Flow)
tools.description: Stabilization terms that make convection-dominated finite-element flow solutions stable: consistent streamline diffusion (GLS/SUPG, also stabilizing P1+P1 pressure) and crosswind diffusion (shock-capturing), which vanish for the exact solution, and inconsistent isotropic diffusion that adds artificial viscosity. The settings apply separately to Navier–Stokes and RANS equations.
tools.usage: spf node > Consistent/Inconsistent Stabilization (Show More Options > Stabilization); Java: physics("spf").prop("ConsistentStabilization").set("CrosswindDiffusion", "0")

parameters.name: StreamlineDiffusion / RANSStreamlineDiffusion
parameters.description: Default on; required for P1+P1.

parameters.name: CrosswindDiffusion / RANSCrosswindDiffusion (ck, ck_RANS)
parameters.description: Default on; tuning constants ck.

parameters.name: IsotropicDiffusion (delid)
parameters.description: prop("InconsistentStabilization"), default off; changes the solution, use only for debugging convergence.

tools.notes: In multiphysics couplings (Nonisothermal Flow, Reacting Flow) the fluid interface controls the coupled stabilization.

tools.name: Pseudo Time Stepping and CFL Control (Fluid Flow)
tools.description: Stationary fluid-flow solves add a pseudo time derivative with a local CFL number that is ramped by a PID controller, turning the nonlinear solve into a robust pseudo-transient march; it is on by default (Automatic) for turbulent, high-Mach, nonisothermal and mixing-plane models. The default solver suggestions use a segregated or fully coupled Newton solver with smoothed-aggregation AMG for large 3D models.
tools.usage: spf node > Advanced Settings > Pseudo Time Stepping; Java: physics("spf").prop("AdvancedSettingProperty").set("PseudoTimeSetting", "On")

parameters.name: PseudoTimeSetting
parameters.description: Automatic (default) | On | Off (UsePseudoTime).

parameters.name: CFLNumbExpr / locCFL
parameters.description: Automatic CFL ramp (spf.localCFLvalue) or a manual expression.

parameters.name: Solver
parameters.description: Segregated (velocity-pressure / turbulence groups) or fully coupled with AMG or geometric multigrid.

tools.notes: Watch the Reciprocal of step size / CFL convergence plot; stalled CFL growth usually indicates mesh or boundary-condition problems.

tools.name: Boundary Layer Mesh for CFD (y+ Guidelines)
tools.description: Meshing guideline for CFD: the physics-controlled mesh of fluid interfaces inserts boundary layers on no-slip walls; low-Re models (SST, k-ω, v2-f, RSM, Spalart–Allmaras, LES low-Re) need the first cell at y+ ≈ 1, while wall functions need y+ ≳ 11 (Delta_wPlus reported in wall units). Swept and structured meshes are efficient in channels, and a mesh convergence study should confirm key quantities.
tools.usage: Mesh > Boundary Layers (Boundary Layer Properties: number of layers, stretching factor, thickness of first layer); Java: model.component("comp1").mesh("mesh1").create("bl1", "BndLayer")

parameters.name: Number of layers
parameters.description: Typically 5-8 for wall functions, 15-25 for low-Re models.

parameters.name: Stretching factor
parameters.description: Growth ratio (1.1-1.3 typical).

parameters.name: Thickness of first layer
parameters.description: Chosen from the target y+ and the estimated friction velocity.

parameters.name: Check
parameters.description: Plot spf.Delta_wPlus on walls (Wall Resolution default plot).

tools.notes: Every Application Library CFD model uses BndLayer/BndLayerProp mesh features (for example CFD_Module/Verification_Examples/ahmed_body).

tools.name: Flow Field Variables (spf.U, spf.sr, spf.vort_magn, spf.cellRe)
tools.description: Postprocessing variables of the single-phase flow interfaces verified in COMSOL 6.4: velocity magnitude spf.U, shear rate spf.sr, vorticity magnitude spf.vort_magn and component spf.vorticityz, cell Reynolds number spf.cellRe, density spf.rho, dynamic and kinematic viscosity spf.mu and spf.nu, absolute pressure spf.pA, viscous dissipation spf.Qvd, divergence spf.divu and CFL-based time step spf.dt_CFL. Dependent variables are u, v, w and p.
tools.usage: Results > any plot > Expression, e.g. spf.U; Java: model.result().numerical("av1").set("expr", new String[]{"spf.U"})

parameters.name: spf.U / u,v,w / p
parameters.description: Velocity magnitude, components and (gauge) pressure.

parameters.name: spf.sr, spf.vort_magn, spf.vorticityz
parameters.description: Shear rate, vorticity magnitude and z-component.

parameters.name: spf.cellRe
parameters.description: Element Reynolds number (mesh resolution indicator).

parameters.name: spf.pA, spf.rho, spf.mu, spf.nu
parameters.description: Absolute pressure and fluid properties.

parameters.name: spf.Qvd, spf.divu, spf.dt_CFL
parameters.description: Viscous dissipation, velocity divergence, CFL time step estimate.

tools.notes: Names verified by evaluation on solved laminar and k-ε models. Replace spf by the interface tag (spf2, ...) when several flow interfaces exist.

tools.name: Total Stress and Drag/Lift Force Evaluation (spf.T_stressx)
tools.description: Forces on walls are obtained by integrating the total stress vector (pressure plus viscous) spf.T_stressx/y/z over the body surface; spf.K_stressx/y/z is the viscous part only. Drag and lift coefficients follow as C_D = F_x/(0.5 ρ U∞² A_ref). Alternatively the reaction force reacf(u) gives the constraint force on no-slip walls.
tools.usage: Results > Derived Values > Surface Integration (3D) / Line Integration (2D) of spf.T_stressx; Java: model.result().numerical().create("int1", "IntSurface")

parameters.name: spf.T_stressx, spf.T_stressy, spf.T_stressz
parameters.description: Total stress (traction) on boundaries, N/m².

parameters.name: spf.K_stressx, ...
parameters.description: Viscous stress components (for skin friction).

parameters.name: reacf(u)
parameters.description: Reaction force density of the velocity constraint (pointwise no-slip).

parameters.name: Sign
parameters.description: The traction acts from the fluid on the boundary oriented by the boundary normal; check sign with a known case.

tools.notes: In 2D the integral gives force per unit depth. For accurate forces use P2+P1 or a well-resolved boundary layer; spf.T_stressx verified in COMSOL 6.4.

tools.name: Wall Resolution and Friction Velocity (spf.Delta_wPlus, spf.u_tau)
tools.description: Boundary variables for turbulent wall treatment: spf.Delta_wPlus is the distance to the first computational point in viscous units (y+) plotted by the default Wall Resolution plot, spf.u_tau is the friction velocity, and spf.delta_w is the wall lift-off distance used by wall functions. Wall shear stress follows from ρ u_tau² or from the viscous stress spf.K_stress components.
tools.usage: Results > Surface/Line plot on walls: spf.Delta_wPlus; Java: model.result("pg2").feature("surf1").set("expr", "spf.Delta_wPlus")

parameters.name: spf.Delta_wPlus
parameters.description: Wall resolution in viscous units; ≈1 needed for Low Re treatment, ≈11.06 and above for wall functions.

parameters.name: spf.u_tau
parameters.description: Friction velocity (wall shear stress τ_w = ρ u_tau²).

parameters.name: spf.delta_w
parameters.description: Wall lift-off in length units (wall functions).

tools.notes: These are boundary variables (defined on walls only); names verified in COMSOL 6.4 on a k-ε model.

tools.name: Turbulence Variables (k, ep, om, spf.nuT, spf.muT)
tools.description: Dependent and derived turbulence variables of RANS interfaces: turbulent kinetic energy k, dissipation rate ep (k-ε), specific dissipation rate om (k-ω, SST), undamped viscosity nutilde (Spalart–Allmaras), plus the turbulent kinematic and dynamic viscosities spf.nuT and spf.muT. The ratio spf.muT/spf.mu indicates how turbulent the flow is.
tools.usage: Results > Expression k, ep, spf.nuT, spf.muT/spf.mu

parameters.name: k, ep, om
parameters.description: Dependent variables (names editable in Dependent Variables section).

parameters.name: spf.nuT, spf.muT
parameters.description: Eddy viscosity.

parameters.name: Reciprocal wall distance
parameters.description: G (wall distance variable) solved in Wall Distance Initialization.

tools.notes: k and ep are not prefixed by spf (verified in COMSOL 6.4); with several turbulent interfaces they get numbered names (k2, ep2).

tools.name: Pressure Drop Evaluation (Surface Average of p)
tools.description: Standard CFD result: the pressure drop of a component is the difference of area-averaged (or mass-flow-weighted) total or static pressure between inlet and outlet. It is obtained with Surface Average derived values, average operators (aveop) defined under Component Couplings, or Global Evaluation of an expression such as aveop_in(p)-aveop_out(p). Parametric sweeps of the inlet velocity then give the system curve.
tools.usage: Definitions > Component Couplings > Average (aveop1 on inlet, aveop2 on outlet); Results > Global Evaluation: aveop1(p)-aveop2(p)

parameters.name: Average operator
parameters.description: Area average; for mass-weighted use intop(spf.rho*u*p)/intop(spf.rho*u).

parameters.name: Total pressure
parameters.description: p + 0.5*spf.rho*spf.U^2 for incompressible flow.

tools.notes: Evaluate far enough from inlets/outlets; include the hydrostatic part consistently when gravity is on.

tools.name: Residence Time and Mean Age of Fluid (Flow Postprocessing)
tools.description: Residence time distributions in reactors, mixers and water-treatment basins are computed either by particle tracing (Particle Tracing for Fluid Flow with an auxiliary time variable or a particle counter) or by solving a mean-age transport equation u·∇τ = ∇·(D∇τ) + 1 with τ = 0 at the inlet, for example with a Transport of Diluted Species interface whose reaction term is 1 and whose concentration is interpreted as age. A pulse tracer in a transient Transport of Diluted Species gives the full RTD curve at the outlet.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Chemical Species Transport > Transport of Diluted Species (tds) using the flow velocity; Reactions: R = 1[mol/(m^3*s)]; Inflow c = 0 at inlet; interpret c [mol/m^3] as age in seconds

parameters.name: Mean age τ
parameters.description: Local mean time since entering the domain.

parameters.name: Diffusion
parameters.description: Include turbulent diffusivity (spf.nuT/ScT) for turbulent flow.

parameters.name: Outlet mean residence time
parameters.description: Flow-weighted average of τ over the outlet.

tools.notes: The CFD Module tutorial on the water purification reactor mentions residence-time analysis as the next step after the turbulent flow solution.

tools.name: Frozen Rotor (study step)
tools.description: Stationary study step for rotating machinery: rotating domains stay frozen at one angle and the rotation enters through centrifugal and Coriolis terms in the rotating frame, while nonrotating domains solve the ordinary stationary equations. It gives a cheap quasi-steady solution of pumps, fans, mixers and turbines and the initial condition for a full Time Dependent sliding-mesh run.
tools.usage: Study > Study Steps > Stationary > Frozen Rotor; Java: model.study("std1").create("frrot", "FrozenRotor")

parameters.name: Rotor position
parameters.description: Defined through the parameter TIME (default 0) that sets the frozen angle.

parameters.name: Physics and variables selection
parameters.description: As for Stationary; can include heat transfer and species.

parameters.name: Auxiliary sweep
parameters.description: Sweep TIME or rotational speed to study rotor-angle dependence.

tools.notes: Requires the CFD Module or Mixer Module. Results depend on the rotor angle when rotor and stator interact strongly.

tools.name: Frozen Rotor with Initialization (study)
tools.description: Preset study for turbulent rotating machinery consisting of a Wall Distance Initialization step followed by a Frozen Rotor step; for 3D High Mach Number Flow with an active Mixing Plane a Mixing Plane Initialization step is inserted in between. It is the default study for Rotating Machinery, Turbulent Flow interfaces.
tools.usage: Add Study > Preset Studies for Selected Physics > Frozen Rotor with Initialization; Java: model.study("std1").create("wdi", "WallDistanceInitialization"); model.study("std1").create("frrot", "FrozenRotor")

parameters.name: Wall Distance Initialization
parameters.description: Solves the reciprocal wall distance needed by the turbulence model.

parameters.name: Frozen Rotor
parameters.description: Stationary rotating-frame solve.

parameters.name: Mixing Plane Initialization
parameters.description: Added automatically when needed.

tools.notes: Requires the CFD Module or Mixer Module.

tools.name: Mixing Plane Initialization (study step)
tools.description: Study step added automatically to Frozen Rotor with Initialization and Stationary with Initialization studies when a Mixing Plane feature is active in 3D High Mach Number Flow models. It performs an initial circumferential mixing of flow and turbulence quantities in the mixing plane before the main solve.
tools.usage: Generated automatically in the study sequence (Frozen Rotor with Initialization / Stationary with Initialization) when Mixing Plane is used

parameters.name: Physics selection
parameters.description: Same flow interface as the subsequent Frozen Rotor/Stationary step.

tools.example:
// 3D compressor stage: High Mach Number Flow, SST + Rotating Domain + Mixing Plane (interior rotor-stator face)
// Add Study > Frozen Rotor with Initialization -> steps: Wall Distance Initialization, Mixing Plane Initialization, Frozen Rotor
tools.notes: Requires the Mixer Module with the CFD Module. Keep pseudo time stepping On when using mixing planes.

tools.name: Frozen Rotor with Stationary Free Surface (study)
tools.description: Preset studies used when a Stationary Free Surface feature is present: a Frozen Rotor step computes the flow with a flat slip surface, then a Wall Distance Initialization-type step evaluates the small free-surface deformation from the linearized free-surface condition including surface tension. A variant with an initial Wall Distance Initialization exists for turbulent models (Frozen Rotor with Initialization and Stationary Free Surface).
tools.usage: Add Study > Frozen Rotor with Stationary Free Surface (or ... with Initialization and Stationary Free Surface); toggle the study window after selecting the free surface to trigger the correct sequence

parameters.name: Frozen Rotor step
parameters.description: Flow solution with slip and constant pressure p_ext on the surface.

parameters.name: Stationary Free Surface step
parameters.description: Computes surface elevation from the frozen-rotor pressure.

tools.example:
// Application Library: Mixer_Module/Tutorials/free_surface_mixer and Mixer_Module/Applications/mixer
// Physics: Rotating Machinery, Turbulent Flow, k-ε + Stationary Free Surface on the liquid top surface
tools.notes: Valid only for small surface deformations; otherwise use a Time Dependent study with Deforming Domain and Free Surface.

tools.name: Phase Initialization (study step)
tools.description: Study step that solves for the reciprocal distance to the initial fluid-fluid interface so that the level set or phase field variable starts as a smooth profile of the correct thickness. It precedes the Time Dependent step in the Time Dependent with Phase Initialization study used by all Two-Phase Flow, Level Set/Phase Field and Ternary models.
tools.usage: Add Study > Time Dependent with Phase Initialization; Java: model.study("std1").create("phasei", "PhaseInitialization"); model.study("std1").create("time", "Transient")

parameters.name: Initial Interface
parameters.description: The boundaries marked by Initial Interface define the zero level.

parameters.name: Settings
parameters.description: Same as a Time Dependent step (solver, physics selection).

tools.notes: Requires the CFD or Microfluidics Module. Verified type string PhaseInitialization.

tools.name: Rotating Machinery, Turbulent Flow Interfaces (spf + Rotating Domain)
tools.description: Mixer Module/CFD Module entries under Fluid Flow > Single-Phase Flow > Rotating Machinery for turbulent flow with Algebraic yPlus, L-VEL, k-ε, realizable k-ε, k-ω, SST, low-Re k-ε, Spalart–Allmaras and v2-f models. Each adds the corresponding Turbulent Flow interface plus a Rotating Domain under Definitions > Moving Mesh, and supports Frozen Rotor or Time Dependent (sliding mesh) studies, non-Newtonian rheology and free surfaces.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Fluid Flow > Single-Phase Flow > Rotating Machinery > Rotating Machinery, Turbulent Flow, k-ε (etc.); Java: physics().create("spf", "TurbulentFlowkeps", "geom1"); common().create("rot1", "RotatingDomain")

parameters.name: Rotating Domain
parameters.description: Rotor domains, rotation axis and rotational velocity (revolutions per time or angular velocity, constant or general).

parameters.name: Flow Continuity pair
parameters.description: Couples rotor and stator across the assembly identity pair.

parameters.name: Study
parameters.description: Frozen Rotor with Initialization, then optionally Time Dependent with Initialization for transient rotor-stator interaction.

tools.notes: Requires the Mixer Module (plus the CFD Module for turbulence). RotatingDomain properties in 6.4 include rotationalVelocityExpression, revolutionsPerTime, angularVelocity, rotationAxis and rotationAxisBasePoint.

tools.name: Stationary Free Surface (Rotating Machinery)
tools.description: Results-processing feature for Frozen Rotor studies that estimates the small deformation of a liquid free surface: the flow is solved with a slip condition and constant pressure p_ext on the surface, then the elevation is computed from the linearized free-surface condition with optional surface tension. It visualizes vortex dips in stirred tanks without a costly moving-mesh transient.
tools.usage: Rotating Machinery flow interface > Stationary Free Surface; Java: physics("spf").create("sfs1", "StationaryFreeSurface", 2)

parameters.name: pext
parameters.description: External (average) pressure on the free surface.

parameters.name: IncludeSurfaceTension
parameters.description: Default 1; coefficient from library (e.g., WaterAir) or user-defined sigma.

parameters.name: SurfaceTensionCoefficient
parameters.description: LibraryCoefficientLiquidGas | LibraryCoefficientLiquidLiquid | LibraryCoefficientLiquidMixtureGas | userdef.

tools.notes: Requires the Mixer Module. With a nonempty selection the default solver switches to geometric multigrid for robustness.

tools.name: Rotating Shaft (Rotating Machinery)
tools.description: Boundary feature for shaft boundaries inside a free-surface (Deforming Domain) region that connect to a Rotating Domain: it prescribes the solid-body rotational velocity of the shaft but uses Navier slip (laminar) or wall functions (turbulent) so the contact line between shaft and free surface can move. It is needed in transient free-surface mixer simulations.
tools.usage: Rotating Machinery flow interface > Rotating Shaft; Java: physics("spf").create("rs1", "RotatingShaft", 2)

parameters.name: AxisOfRotation
parameters.description: xAxis, yAxis, zAxis (default) or userdef (rotaxbp, rotaxdir).

parameters.name: RotationalFrequency
parameters.description: RevolutionsPerTime (rpm) or AngularVelocity (w).

parameters.name: RotationalDirection
parameters.description: PositiveAngularVelocity or NegativeAngularVelocity.

tools.notes: Requires the Mixer Module. Low-Re wall treatment is not allowed on the shaft.

tools.name: Mixing Plane (Rotating Machinery)
tools.description: Interior boundary condition between rotating and nonrotating domains that circumferentially averages flow, turbulence and wall distance quantities, giving a steady representation of rotor-stator interaction for sector models of turbines, compressors and pumps. It works in Stationary, Frozen Rotor, Wall Distance Initialization and Mixing Plane Initialization steps and supports axial or radial flow configurations.
tools.usage: Rotating Machinery flow interface > Mixing Plane (interior face) or Mixing Plane (Pair); Java: physics("spf").create("mp1", "MixingPlane", 2)

parameters.name: Edge where mixing is consolidated
parameters.description: One bounding edge of the mixing plane (3D).

parameters.name: Axis definition (item.r0, item.axis, item.er)
parameters.description: Origin, rotation axis and radial direction.

parameters.name: item.flowDirection
parameters.description: axial or radial.

tools.notes: Requires the Mixer Module. Suitable for sectors (not full 360° geometries); keep pseudo time stepping On.

tools.name: Mixer Module Part Library (Tanks and Impellers)
tools.description: Parameterized geometry parts for stirred vessels: dished-, flat- and cone-bottom tanks with optional baffles, a straight shaft and eleven impellers (five axial such as pitched blade and propeller, four radial such as Rushton turbine and Smith/backswept impellers, and two for highly viscous fluids such as anchor). Blades can be infinitely thin surfaces or solids (solids require the Design Module).
tools.usage: Geometry > Parts > Part Libraries > Mixer Module > Tanks / Impellers (Axial, Radial, Viscous); set part parameters in the Part Instance node

parameters.name: d_ta, d_im, hp_im
parameters.description: Tank diameter, impeller diameter, impeller position.

parameters.name: n_ib, ap_ib
parameters.description: Number of blades and blade pitch angle.

parameters.name: pa_rd_im, pa_ud_im
parameters.description: Blade direction (clockwise/counterclockwise) and vertical flip.

parameters.name: d_cs_pr, pa_cs_pr
parameters.description: Cross-section planes for power draw and flow number evaluation.

tools.notes: Requires the Mixer Module. The parts create selections (rotating domain, impeller boundaries) that simplify physics setup.
